metadata.title: A model for the enhanced production rate of early-type hypervelocity stars in the Galactic halo

evidence.quote: the observation of the GC-origin HVS1
which agrees with the observation of the GC-origin HVS1

notes: HVS1 (called “GC-origin HVS1” at T:p6-b4) is the only individually named star. The paper uses its observed 45 ± 32 Myr timescale as an external benchmark for the model rather than newly selecting or analyzing it, so it is recorded as follow-up. No Gaia ID or other alias is supplied. The collective HVS population mentioned at T:p1-b10 is not individually identified, so its members are not listed.

HVS1: The only mention of the target star HVS1 in the supplied text is at T:p6-b4: "which agrees with the observation of the GC-origin HVS1 (45 ± 32 Myr; W. R. Brown et al. 2012)". This is a flight time (ejection age) quoted from W. R. Brown et al. (2012), which is not one of the requested quantity identifiers (ra, dec, distance, parallax, proper motions, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, bound/unbound probability). The Letter itself is a theoretical population model of the 500 Myr NSC disk and reports no positional, kinematic, or probability measurements for HVS1. Therefore no quantity is retained.
